mainTopic: The meaning of "זֶה הַדָּבָר": the one-generation limit, the גזרה שוה between נדרים and שחוטי חוץ, and how בית שמאי read it
overview: Earlier, the גמרא learned from the words "זֶה הַדָּבָר" that the rule limiting whom בנות צלפחד could marry applied only to their generation. רבה זוטי asks רב אשי why the same words at the start of the laws of נדרים do not limit vows to one generation as well. רב אשי answers that in נדרים the words are needed for a גזרה שוה with שחוטי חוץ. In the inheritance parsha, the words would be extra unless they teach a one-generation limit. A ברייתא spells out the גזרה שוה in both directions. From the first direction, רב אחא בר יעקב learns that three ordinary people (הדיוטות) can release a vow, and "ראשי המטות" adds that one expert alone can also do it. From the second direction, רב ששת learns that a חכם can undo a הקדש. בית שמאי hold that a הקדש cannot be undone, so they use each "זה הדבר" for its own lesson. The גמרא then asks where they learn the rule of three ordinary people, and begins a ברייתא of רבי יוסי הגלילי on the festivals פסוק that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do the laws of vows also apply only to that generation?
steps.stepSummary: The words "זֶה הַדָּבָר" also open the parsha of נדרים, so the questioner asks whether those laws were also limited to one generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The parsha of vows also says 'This is the matter,' addressed to the heads of the tribes. So should vows also apply only in that generation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier reasoning by pointing to another place where the same words "זֶה הַדָּבָר" appear: the laws of vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, "זֶה הַדָּבָר" was read as meaning 'this matter, only for this generation.' If that reading is right, the same words in the parsha of נדרים should limit those laws too. That cannot be true, because the laws of vows clearly apply forever.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is the matter": the phrase being discussed
The heads of the tribes, to whom the parsha of vows was said
This generation only
Applies, is in effect

phrases.english: "This is the matter" of the heads of the tribes:
is it also so that it should not apply
phrases.notes: The words 'it should not apply... except in this generation' copy how the גמרא read the same phrase earlier, about בנות צלפחד.

phrases.english: except in this generation?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא יְהֵא נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בְּדוֹר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading of "זֶה הַדָּבָר" as a one-generation limit, which was made before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that "זֶה הַדָּבָר" limits a law to one generation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear in the parsha of נדרים, which surely applies forever. So the words alone cannot mean 'only this generation.'

steps.title: In vows, the phrase is used for a link to another parsha
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that in the parsha of נדרים, "זה" is used for a גזרה שוה with the parsha of שחוטי חוץ, so it does not mean 'this generation only.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: in that case, we learn 'this' from 'this' in another place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the words in the parsha of vows do not limit those laws to one generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the parsha of vows, the word "זה" is already busy: it connects vows to the parsha of animals slaughtered outside the משכן (שחוטי חוץ), which applies forever. Since the word has that job, it is not read as 'this generation only.'

keyTerms.meaning: Learns, derives
From there, from another parsha
Sacrifices slaughtered outside the משכן or בית המקדש

phrases.english: He said to him: That one,
learns "this" from "this" there.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the פסוק about slaughtering outside the משכן, which also says "זה הדבר" (ויקרא 17:2).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: in נדרים the phrase is used for a גזרה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "זֶה הַדָּבָר" in נדרים should limit vows to one generation, just as with בנות צלפחד.
steps.terutzMaskana: In נדרים, "זה" links to שחוטי חוץ, a law for all generations, so there is no limit.

steps.title: Why not use the same link for the daughters' case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if "זה" can be linked to שחוטי חוץ, why not link it that way for בנות צלפחד too, and make that law apply forever?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then this case too should learn 'this' from 'this' in that other place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the same link could also be used for the parsha of בנות צלפחד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גזרה שוה with שחוטי חוץ shows that a law applies forever, it could do the same for the inheritance parsha. Then we would have no proof that the בנות צלפחד rule was only for one generation.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
Let it learn, let it derive

phrases.english: This one too,
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the parsha of בנות צלפחד.

phrases.english: let it learn "this" from "this" there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אשי's answer in step 2 against the original reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of "זֶה הַדָּבָר" in the parsha of בנות צלפחד as 'only this generation'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same גזרה שוה could be applied there, which would make that law apply forever too.

steps.title: In the daughters' case the words would be extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the parshiyos of נדרים and שחוטי חוץ the words were needed for a גזרה שוה. In the inheritance parsha they have no other job, so they must be teaching 'only this generation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of question is that? There, the words were needed for a גזרה שוה. Here, why were they needed? The Torah could have said nothing, and I would know on my own that the law is for all generations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and explains why "זֶה הַדָּבָר" in the בנות צלפחד parsha really does mean 'this generation only.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every law in the Torah applies forever unless the Torah says otherwise. So if the Torah wanted the בנות צלפחד rule to be permanent, it did not need to say anything. Since it added "זֶה הַדָּבָר" and there is no גזרה שוה for the words to serve there, they must be teaching a limit to one generation.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? (a way of brushing off a comparison)
Granted, it makes sense that...
Was needed
A link between two parshiyos that share the same word
For all generations

steps.whatToRemember: When the Torah's words are not needed for anything else, the גמרא reads them as teaching something new. Here that new thing is that the בנות צלפחד rule was only for that generation.

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted there, it was needed for a גזרה שוה;
here, what was it needed for?
Let the verse be silent about it,
and I would know that it is for all generations!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם, אִיצְטְרִיךְ לִגְזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: where the phrase has no other job, it teaches the one-generation limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same גזרה שוה could make the בנות צלפחד law permanent.
steps.terutzMaskana: A permanent law needs no words to say so. The extra phrase here can only mean 'only this generation.'

steps.title: Which גזרה שוה is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the גזרה שוה between נדרים and שחוטי חוץ teaches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks to see the actual גזרה שוה it has been relying on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole answer depended on the words being 'needed' for a גזרה שוה. The גמרא now wants to show what that גזרה שוה teaches, to prove the words really are needed there.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What is the גזרה שוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the גזרה שוה that was mentioned in steps 2 and 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the "זה"/"זה" גזרה שוה between נדרים and שחוטי חוץ teaches

steps.title: The ברייתא linking vows and slaughtering outside
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that each parsha lends something to the other. Vows, like שחוטי חוץ, apply to אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל. שחוטי חוץ, like vows, involves the heads of the tribes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: Here it says 'This is the matter,' and there it says 'This is the matter.' Just as there it means אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל, so too here. And just as here it means the heads of the tribes, so too there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that spells out the גזרה שוה in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parsha of שחוטי חוץ is addressed to אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל. The parsha of vows is addressed to the heads of the tribes. The גזרה שוה lets each parsha borrow the other's audience, so the words really are needed in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Here (the parsha of vows)
There (the parsha of שחוטי חוץ)
Just as... so too: the pattern of a comparison

phrases.english: As it is taught: It is said here: "This is the matter,"
and it is said there: "This is the matter";
phrases.notes: 'There' is ויקרא 17:2, about slaughtering outside the משכן.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן – אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: just as there it is Aaron and his sons and all Israel,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן – אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so too here it is Aaron and his sons and all Israel.
And just as here it is the heads of the tribes,
so too there it is the heads of the tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן: ״זֶה הַדָּבָר״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן: ״זֶה הַדָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A two-way גזרה שוה: vows apply to אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל, and שחוטי חוץ involves the heads of the tribes.

steps.title: What practical law does the first half teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first half of the ברייתא and asks what practical law comes from saying vows apply to אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: just as there it means אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל, so too here. What law does that teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to one line of the ברייתא and asks what it means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone already knows that all Jews can make vows. So saying that vows apply to 'all of ישראל' seems to teach nothing new, and the גמרא wants to know what practical point it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: introduces a quote from the source just cited
For what law? What is the practical point?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: מָה לְהַלָּן אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Master said: Just as there it is Aaron and his sons and all Israel,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so too here it is Aaron and his sons and all Israel.
For what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מָה לְהַלָּן אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו וְכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes apart the first half of the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law taught by connecting vows to 'אהרן, his sons and all of ישראל'

steps.title: Three ordinary people can release a vow
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that the גזרה שוה teaches that a vow can be released by three ordinary people (הדיוטות). It does not need experts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: It teaches that releasing vows can be done by three ordinary people.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the practical law behind the first half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parsha of vows mentions 'heads of the tribes,' which might suggest that only important experts can release a vow. The link to 'all of ישראל' teaches that ordinary people are also fit, as long as there are three of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Releasing or cancelling vows
Ordinary people, not experts or judges
Three

steps.whatToRemember: The 'heads of the tribes' in the parsha of vows does not limit releasing vows to experts. Through the גזרה שוה, three ordinary people can release a vow.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not about a husband or father cancelling a vow. It is about releasing a vow through a group of three.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
To say that the releasing of vows is done by three ordinary people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: לוֹמַר שֶׁהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A vow can be released by three ordinary people (הדיוטות).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה: releasing a vow does not need expert judges, only three ordinary people.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'heads of the tribes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב: the vows parsha mentions ראשי המטות, so how can ordinary people release a vow?
steps.simpleTranslation: But "the heads of the tribes" is written in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 8. If the vows parsha speaks to the heads of the tribes, it sounds like only important leaders can release vows, not three ordinary people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said that three הדיוטות can release a vow. But the פסוק in פרשת מטות opens with the words ראשי המטות, which suggests that experts or leaders are required. The גמרא wants to know what that phrase is doing if ordinary people are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The heads of the tribes (the opening words of the vows parsha)
Ordinary people, not experts
But look! (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But "the heads of the tribes"
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:2, the opening of the vows parsha.

phrases.english: is written in it!
phrases.notes: He means in the vows parsha, which seems to require leaders, not ordinary people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תשובה of רב אחא בר יעקב in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that three הדיוטות can release a vow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק names ראשי המטות, which implies that leaders or experts are needed.

steps.title: The heads of the tribes means one expert alone
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא in the name of רבי יוחנן, the גמרא explains that ראשי המטות teaches that a single expert can release a vow by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it refers to a single expert. Here too, it refers to a single expert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ראשי המטות does not cancel the rule of three ordinary people. It adds a second rule: one expert can release a vow all alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to release a vow. Three הדיוטות can do it, or one יחיד מומחה can do it. The phrase ראשי המטות is the source for the second way, so it does not argue against Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: A single expert in halacha
An אמורא who passes on this teaching
The אמורא who said this teaching first
So too, the same here

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
with a single expert;
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's teaching from elsewhere: the heads of the tribes stand for one expert.

phrases.english: so too here, with a single expert.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the phrase to a different law, so both rules stand side by side.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראשי המטות means only leaders can release vows, so three ordinary people would not be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: ראשי המטות teaches that one expert alone can release a vow. Three ordinary people can also do it.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow can be released either by three ordinary people or by one expert alone.

steps.title: What do the heads of the tribes teach about שחוטי חוץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second half of the ברייתא and asks what practical law comes from linking the heads of the tribes to שחוטי חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And just as here it says the heads of the tribes, so too there it means the heads of the tribes." For what law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second half of the ברייתא from Step 6. It asks what practical difference it makes that the heads of the tribes are connected to שחוטי חוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked this question about the first half of the ברייתא. Now the גמרא asks the same thing about the other direction of the גזרה שוה. What does the law of slaughtering outside the בית המקדש have to do with the heads of the tribes?

keyTerms.meaning: There, in the other parsha
For what practical law?
Offerings slaughtered outside the משכן or בית המקדש

phrases.english: And just as here, the heads of the tribes,
so too there, the heads of the tribes.
For what law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה כָּאן רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת אַף לְהַלָּן רָאשֵׁי הַמַּטּוֹת לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the first half of the ברייתא (Steps 7-10) to its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law the link between ראשי המטות and שחוטי חוץ teaches.

steps.title: A הקדש can be undone like a vow
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the גזרה שוה teaches that a person can ask a חכם to undo a הקדש, just as he can for a vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: it is to teach that there is שאלה for הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the practical law. Just as a חכם can undo a vow, a חכם can also undo a declaration that made something הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heads of the tribes stand for the power of a חכם to undo a vow. Linking that phrase to the parsha of offerings shows that this same power works on consecrated things. So someone who regrets making an animal הקדש can ask a חכם to cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a חכם to undo a vow or declaration
Something set aside as holy for the בית המקדש
The אמורא who gives this answer

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
To say that there is asking for release of consecration.
phrases.notes: Literally "there is asking in הקדש": a person may go to a חכם and have his הקדש cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לוֹמַר שֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁאֵלָה בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גזרה שוה teaches that a חכם can undo a הקדש, just like a vow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question. Not everyone agrees that a הקדש can be undone.

steps.title: What do בית שמאי do with 'this' and 'this'?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold that a הקדש cannot be undone, so they cannot use the גזרה שוה for רב ששת's lesson. What do they learn from the two words "זה"?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בית שמאי, who say there is no שאלה for הקדש, as we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say a mistaken הקדש is still הקדש, and בית הלל say it is not הקדש. What do they do with this "זה" and that "זה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רב ששת's answer. According to בית שמאי, a הקדש can never be cancelled. If so, what are the matching words "זה" in the two parshiyos teaching them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof that בית שמאי reject שאלה on הקדש is their view that even a mistaken הקדש stays holy. If even a mistake does not undo it, then asking a חכם cannot undo it either. That leaves the matching words "זה" with no job for them, so the גמרא asks what they learn from those words.

keyTerms.meaning: The students of שמאי
The students of הלל, who often argue with בית שמאי
A הקדש made by mistake
As we learned in a משנה
What do they do with it? (what do they learn from it)

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not arguing about the heads of the tribes directly. Their view on a mistaken הקדש simply shows that, for them, a הקדש cannot be undone.

phrases.english: And according to Beit Shammai, who say:
there is no asking for release of consecration,
as we learned: Beit Shammai say:
consecration in error is consecration,
and Beit Hillel say: it is not consecration;
this "this" and "this"
phrases.notes: The "זה הדבר" in each parsha: the words used for the גזרה שוה.

phrases.english: what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי דְּאָמְרִי אֵין שְׁאֵלָה בְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer from the point of view of בית שמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of "זה" / "זה" for a גזרה שוה teaching שאלה on הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי hold that a הקדש cannot be undone, so for them the matching words seem to have no purpose.

steps.title: For בית שמאי, each 'זה הדבר' teaches its own lesson
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי use "זה הדבר" in שחוטי חוץ to exclude pinching a bird's neck. They use "זה הדבר" in the vows parsha to split the powers of the חכם and the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: The "זה הדבר" of שחוטי חוץ is needed to teach that one is liable for slaughtering but not for pinching. The "זה הדבר" of the heads of the tribes is needed to teach that a חכם can release a vow and a husband cannot, and that a husband can cancel a vow and a חכם cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי do not use these words for a גזרה שוה at all. Each "זה" teaches its own separate law in its own parsha.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שחוטי חוץ, "זה" narrows the punishment to real slaughtering. Pinching a bird's neck outside the בית המקדש does not bring that punishment. In the vows parsha, "זה" limits each person to his own power: התרה belongs only to the חכם, and הפרה belongs only to the husband.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is the matter" (the phrase in both parshiyos)
One who kills a bird by pinching its neck with a fingernail
A חכם releases (undoes) a vow
A husband cancels his wife's vow
He needs it (for another lesson)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא, as רב ששת explains it, uses "זה" / "זה" for a גזרה שוה. בית שמאי use each "זה" for its own lesson: slaughtering but not pinching, and חכם מתיר versus בעל מפר.

phrases.english: "This is the matter" of offerings slaughtered outside —
they need it
"For slaughtering he is liable,"
"but he is not liable for pinching."
"This is the matter" of the heads of the tribes —
they need it for: "A sage releases,"
but a husband does not release.
A husband cancels, but a sage does not cancel."
phrases.notes: Two different words: מתיר is what a חכם does, and מפר is what a husband does. Each one has only his own power.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word is given its own separate lesson, so no גזרה שוה is needed for בית שמאי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For בית שמאי, the words "זה" / "זה" would have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: In שחוטי חוץ, "זה" excludes pinching. In the vows parsha, "זה" separates the power of the חכם from the power of the husband.

steps.title: Where do בית שמאי learn the rule of three laymen?
steps.stepSummary: Since בית שמאי do not use the גזרה שוה, the גמרא asks what source they have for releasing vows through three הדיוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to בית שמאי, who do not use this גזרה שוה, where do they learn that a vow can be released by three ordinary people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about בית שמאי's opinion. They do not use the verbal link, so what is their source for three ordinary people releasing a vow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 showed that בית שמאי use both "זה הדבר" phrases for other lessons, so they do not use them for the גזרה שוה. That leaves a gap. They still agree that three הדיוטות can release a vow, so they need a different source for that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
Undoing vows. Here it means a vow being released by others.
Ordinary people who are not experts
From where do they know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.aramaic: וּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי דְּלֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: And according to Beit Shammai, who do not have the verbal analogy,
phrases.notes: This is the "זה הדבר" link from the last few steps. בית שמאי used both phrases for other lessons.

phrases.english: dissolution of vows by three laymen,
from where do they derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי דְּלֵית לְהוּ גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 14. Since בית שמאי used the "זה הדבר" phrases for other lessons, the גמרא now asks where they get the rule of three laymen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source בית שמאי use for releasing vows through three ordinary people.

steps.title: They learn it from a ברייתא on the festivals פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says בית שמאי learn it from a ברייתא on the פסוק "וידבר משה את מעדי ה׳", and it begins quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from what was taught in a ברייתא: "And משה told the appointed festivals of ה׳ to the children of Israel." רבי יוסי הגלילי says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by pointing to a ברייתא about a פסוק on the festivals. This is a setup line. The actual teaching of רבי יוסי הגלילי comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not use the "זה הדבר" words at all. It uses a different פסוק, the last פסוק of the festival section in ויקרא. How this פסוק connects to releasing vows will become clear once רבי יוסי הגלילי's words are quoted.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי learn the rule from a ברייתא explaining ויקרא 23:44. רבי יוסי הגלילי's explanation follows in the next section.
